Name: Oak
Description: Sturdy, reliable wood. The backbone of simple construction.
ClimateCycle: Garden sun — the deep-rooted standard
CraftPairing: With Willow — the door and the lean; the Garden Path's pair
CraftProperty: Dense, hard, the lightning tree — the strike is the proof
RitualRole: THE THRESHOLD WOOD — doors and door posts; the oath wood; the god-touched (the strike made it the wood you swear on)

Name: Willow
Description: Flexible wood that bends without breaking. Used for woven structures.
ClimateCycle: Garden sun and water — the leaning-over-water bank
CraftPairing: With Rose and Thyme — the Garden Path's mourning-tea trio
CraftProperty: Bends without breaking; the bark carries the willow's own chemistry (the precursor the modern painkiller came from)
RitualRole: THE GRIEF WOOD — the moon's tree; wreaths and mourning work; the bend that survives the flood. Bridges two pillars: the wood in ritual, the bark in remedy

Name: Pine
Description: Soft, fragrant wood. The staple of Norse construction.

Name: Cypress
Description: Water-resistant wood from the swamp. Naturally rot-proof.
ClimateCycle: Bayou humidity — the humid air and the standing water
CraftPairing: With Bog Oak and Spanish Moss — the Bayou Bridge corridor's trio
CraftProperty: Does not rot in water; endures the wet for centuries
RitualRole: THE CROSSING WOOD — planted in graveyards, carved for what must last through both worlds; the wood that endures where the water keeps

Name: Birch
Description: Pale, smooth bark wood. Used for writing and light construction.

Name: Bamboo
Description: Fast-growing, incredibly strong. The architectural backbone of the East.
ClimateCycle: China — the monsoon push; the grove's own rhythm
CraftPairing: With Lacquer and Silk — the China craft trio's frame; with Reed — the weaver's pair
CraftProperty: Grass, not wood — hollow-jointed, tensile; stronger in tension than steel of the same weight; the fastest growth in the building world (a season, not a century)
RitualRole: THE SWIFT WOOD — the scaffold, the flute, the brush handle; the Patience Wood's opposite (the olive's decade, the bamboo's season); the hollow that becomes the vessel

Name: Sandalwood
Description: Fragrant sacred wood. Used in temples and ceremonial structures.

Name: Teak
Description: Dense, oily hardwood. Weatherproof and beautiful. Worth the journey.

Name: OliveWood
Description: Twisted, grained hardwood. The wood of ancient civilizations.
ClimateCycle: Greece — the dry warmth and the limestone; the tree that thrives where rain is scarce
CraftPairing: With Marble — Greece's pair (the table and the oil); with Heather honey — the Mediterranean larder
CraftProperty: Twisted grain that never splits true; the tree that lives a thousand years and keeps fruiting; the oil that is the lamp's light and the anointing
RitualRole: THE PATIENCE WOOD — a decade before the first fruit, a century before the full harvest; the old-grove wood; the hearth of the Mediterranean

Name: EnglishOak
Description: Dense, noble wood from the ancient forests of Camelot.
ClimateCycle: Camelot — the oath ground's deep loam
CraftPairing: With Yew — Camelot's churchyard pair
CraftProperty: The same oak, grown slow on oath ground — the densest grain of the family
RitualRole: THE OATH WOOD — Camelot's own, the Round Table's kin; thresholds sworn on; the table's ruling grain

Name: AndeanAlder
Description: High-altitude wood from the mountains. Light and resilient.

Name: BogOak
Description: Ancient oak preserved in the Irish bog for millennia. Black, dense, heavy with time.
ClimateCycle: Bayou water — the anaerobic keeping; the tannins are the preservative
CraftPairing: With Cypress — the fallen and the standing
CraftProperty: Fell and was KEPT — the water turned the grain dark and dense; time did the crafting
RitualRole: THE MEMORY WOOD — ritual pieces meant to outlive their maker; the River City's petrified kin

Name: Yew
Description: The wood of bows and longbows. Sacred, poisonous, enduring.
ClimateCycle: Camelot — the churchyard's deep shade; the slow centuries
CraftPairing: With English Oak — the oath and the guardian; Camelot's churchyard pair
CraftProperty: The longest-lived tree of the old world — every part is poison except the berry's flesh; the spring that made the longbow
RitualRole: THE PASSAGE WOOD — the churchyard tree planted among the graves (the poison guards the dead); the bow's spring; Camelot's guardian tree — in the Round Table's own recipe and the Final Room's

Name: Luminwood
Description: Wood that glows with internal light. Only grows in the Fae Kingdom. Living wood that never stops growing.

Name: Redwood
Description: Massive, fire-resistant wood from the tallest trees on earth.

Name: Chestnut
Description: Near-extinct wood. Rare, beautiful grain. A relic of forests past.

Name: CanopyWood
Description: Light, flexible wood from the treetops. Grown in sunlight and wind.

Name: Juniper
Description: Twisted, aromatic desert wood. Hard as stone, scented as incense.

Name: DesertIronwood
Description: The densest wood in North America. Sinks in water. Worth the desert crossing.

Name: ShadowWood
Description: Wood from trees that never see the sun. Pale, cold, slightly luminous.

Name: LodgepolePine
Description: Straight, slender trunks. The teepee wood, the lodge wood.

Name: Sandstone
Description: Granular, warm-toned stone. The building block of the pyramids.
LiveValues: {"Description": "Sand compressed by pressure — the layered stone of ancient temples.", "Zone": "Campgrounds", "Category": "building", "Rarity": "uncommon", "Base44Id": "6aa23879cd9fd41196298ff0", "CreatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000", "UpdatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000"}

Name: Limestone
Description: Soft, pale stone. The foundation of castles and cathedrals.

Name: PetrifiedWood
Description: Wood turned to stone over millions of years. The bridge between wood and mineral.

Name: Runestone
Description: Stone that holds runes. It hums when touched by someone who knows the old words.

Name: Granite
Description: Hard, speckled, unyielding. The mountain's backbone.

Name: Obsidian
Description: Black volcanic glass. Sharp enough to split a hair, dark enough to see the void.
LiveValues: {"Description": "Magma quenched by water — volcanic glass, sharp as ritual, dark as the deep.", "Zone": "Campgrounds", "Category": "compound", "Rarity": "rare", "Base44Id": "6aa23879cd9fd41196298fed", "CreatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000", "UpdatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000"}

Name: Andesite
Description: Volcanic stone. The Inca built with this — fitting stones so tight no blade can pass.

Name: Marble
Description: Crystalline, luminous stone. The sculptor's dream.

Name: Agate
Description: Banded, colorful stone. The fossil forest's gift.

Name: AbyssalStone
Description: Stone from the bottom of the ocean. Heavy with the pressure of miles of water.

Name: Crystal
Description: Pure geode crystal from the heart of the Inn. The Inn's namesake material.
LiveValues: {"Description": "Glass refined by fire again — ordered structure, resonant clarity.", "Zone": "Campgrounds", "Category": "refined", "Rarity": "rare", "Base44Id": "6aa23879cd9fd41196298fea", "CreatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000", "UpdatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000"}

Name: Turquoise
Description: Blue-green stone of the desert Southwest. Sky made solid.

Name: AncientBrick
Description: Roman-era brick. The bones of the old world, stacked and forgotten.

Name: BogIron
Description: Iron pulled from the bog. The first metal humanity learned to work.

Name: Bronze
Description: The alloy that named an age. Stronger than copper, beautiful as gold.

Name: Copper
Description: Malleable, warm-toned metal. The conductor, the bridge.

Name: DeepSeaCrystal
Description: Crystal that forms under impossible pressure. Glows with its own internal ocean.

Name: Silver
Description: Moonlight metal. The alchemist's conductor.

Name: StarIron
Description: Iron from fallen stars. The only metal that can work cosmic crystal.

Name: GoldOre
Description: Raw gold from the Andes. The Inca called it the sweat of the sun.

Name: DesertGlass
Description: Glass forged by lightning striking desert sand. The pharaohs' treasure.

Name: SpanishMoss
Description: Draped from cypress branches. The bayou's lace curtain.
ClimateCycle: Bayou humidity — the air itself is the water; takes all its water from the air, not the ground
CraftPairing: With Cypress — it only grows where cypress holds it
CraftProperty: The air-root — no soil needed; the epiphyte that drinks the sky
RitualRole: THE CATCHER — the moss that catches what the air carries; the Bog Fairy Golem's frequency catcher, the thatching and the veil

Name: BogMoss
Description: Spongy, water-holding moss from the bog floor. Preserves what it covers.

Name: FairySilk
Description: Silk spun by Fae creatures. Shimmers between colors. Stronger than spider silk.

Name: Reed
Description: River reed. The first writing surface, the first woven mat, the first raft.

Name: Papyrus
Description: The paper of the ancients. Knowledge made portable.

Name: Nightshade
Description: Beautiful, deadly. The poisoner's garden treasure.
ClimateCycle: Shade — the alkaloids the sun would burn away; the poison plants are the shade's plants
CraftPairing: Never beside the gentle herbs — the garden's one warning pair
CraftProperty: The poison and the pupil-dilator are the same plant at different amounts — DOSE IS THE DIFFERENCE between medicine and harm
RitualRole: The Poison Garden's own lesson: respect, not fear — the dose law's teacher

Name: Fern
Description: Ancient plant. Older than flowers, older than trees. The forest floor's lace.

Name: Ginseng
Description: The root of life. Worth its weight in gold in the mountains.
ClimateCycle: Appalachian frost cycle — the winter IS the ingredient; the cold makes the potency
CraftPairing: With Fern — the mountain floor's pair
CraftProperty: The adaptogen the frost MAKES — the cold cycle is the potency; greenhouse ginseng is a different, lesser thing
RitualRole: The mountain's root — the thin-soil strength; the frost-earned medicine

Name: Amber
Description: Sunlight trapped in tree resin. The Norse called it the tears of Freya.

Name: ThornVine
Description: Vines that grow thorns as defense. Beautiful and dangerous.

Name: Honey
Description: Liquid gold from the meadery. Preserves anything it touches.

Name: Beeswax
Description: Clean-burning, sweet-scented. The candle maker's foundation.

Name: Pearl
Description: Born from irritation. The ocean's gem, formed in darkness.

Name: Coral
Description: Living stone. Built by tiny creatures over centuries.

Name: Lacquer
Description: Tree sap refined into a hard, glossy finish. The art of the East.

Name: GeyserSalt
Description: Salt from geothermal formations. Pure, mineral-rich, crystalline.

Name: ResonanceCrystal
Description: Geode crystal tuned to 42Hz. The Inn's frequency made solid.

Name: FaeDust
Description: Residue of Fae passage. Glows, drifts, and vanishes if not caught quickly.

Name: Luminite
Description: Mineral that stores Fae light. The magical equivalent of a battery.

Name: GhostCrystal
Description: Crystal formed where spirits pass. Cold to the touch. Whispers when held.

Name: CosmicCrystal
Description: Crystal that fell from the stars. Contains the same elements as the Inn's foundation.

Name: DragonScale
Description: Shed by the dragon kittens. Scales that hold warmth for days. Near-impossible to obtain.

Name: StarDust
Description: Dust from the space between stars. Must be gathered with a crystal net on the cosmology level.

Name: BakedBrick
Description: Clay bricks fired in kilns to resist water. Durable enough for city walls and ziggurat exteriors.

Name: Clay
Description: River clay pressed into mudbricks and sun-dried. The foundational building material of Mesopotamia.
LiveValues: {"Description": "Fine-grained earth — shaped by hand, hardened by fire. The potter's origin.", "Zone": "Campgrounds", "Category": "raw", "Rarity": "common", "Base44Id": "6aa23879cd9fd41196298fe3", "CreatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000", "UpdatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000"}

Name: Bitumen
Description: Natural asphalt from the earth. Used as waterproof mortar, sealant, and adhesive for millennia.

Name: Silk
Description: Woven silk from cultivated silkworms. Window scrims, canopies, and interior dividers.

Name: Saguaro
Description: Ribs from fallen saguaro cacti. Used as roof laths (latillas) in desert construction.

Name: LapisLazuli
Description: Deep blue stone imported from ancient trade routes. Ground into pigment for the Ishtar Gate.

Name: Jade
Description: Carved decorative stone denoting nobility and purity. Inlaid into screens, lintels, and furniture.

Name: CaveMushroom
Description: Fungal growth from the cave floors. Medicinal, edible, and used for insulation.

Name: GlowMoss
Description: Bioluminescent moss that grows in total darkness. The cave's natural light source.

Name: CavePearl
Description: Pearl-like formations from mineral-rich cave water. Decoration and trade goods.

Name: Basalt
Description: Volcanic stone that fractures into hexagonal columns. The Vorticist's geometry made solid. Angular, dark, precise.

Name: CalciumCrystal
Description: Crystallized calcium from ancient bone deposits. The mineral that bones become over millennia. A stone that was once alive.

Name: Bone
Description: Bones found naturally exposed across the Inn's zones. The last structure the body builds. O'Keeffe's architecture of what remains.

Name: AmberCrystal
Description: The Inn's own amber crystals. Hold warm light and hum at 42Hz. Used as lamp fuel and light source in the caves.

Name: SaltCrystal
Description: Salt crystals from evaporated seawater in the cave pools. Preserves anything it touches.

Name: SeaGlass
Description: Glass smoothed by centuries of tidal action. Frost-edged, sea-colored, sharp only at the molecular level.

Name: TidalMoss
Description: Moss that grows where the tide meets the stone. Survives saltwater and freshwater. The amphibious plant.

Name: UndercityIron
Description: Iron smelted in the Undercity's workshops. Darker than surface iron. Holds an edge longer. The metal of the inventors.

Name: BioluminescentAlgae
Description: Blue-green algae that glows in the dark water. The Tidal Caves' underwater light source. Vorticist color in living form.

Name: ShadowMoss
Description: Moss that thrives in total darkness. Absorbs sound and light. The catacomb's quiet is this moss.

Name: GargoyleStone
Description: Stone with awareness. The Ent's senses embedded in the architecture. Watches, listens, remembers. The 64Hz Listener lives in this stone.

Name: VenomSac
Description: Venom harvested from the Poison Garden's creatures. Used in alchemy, preservation, and dark crafting.

Name: Fossil
Description: Ancient preserved remains — ammonites, trilobites, fern impressions. Found in sedimentary layers throughout the catacombs.
LiveValues: {"Description": "Life preserved in stone by time — the archive of what was, read in the rock.", "Zone": "Campgrounds", "Category": "compound", "Rarity": "rare", "Base44Id": "6aa23879cd9fd41196298ff5", "CreatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000", "UpdatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000"}

Name: FogMoss
Description: Pale grey-green moss that thrives in perpetual coastal fog. Damp, cool, used for binding and insulation.

Name: Chalcedony
Description: Botryoidal microcrystalline quartz with waxy luster. Pale blue-gray with translucent edges. Grows in volcanic cavities.

Name: Slate
Description: Fine-grained metamorphic rock that splits into thin sheets. Used for roofing tiles and writing tablets.
LiveValues: {"Description": "Clay compressed by pressure — the roofing stone, the writing surface.", "Zone": "Campgrounds", "Category": "building", "Rarity": "uncommon", "Base44Id": "6aa23879cd9fd41196298ff2", "CreatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000", "UpdatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000"}

Name: Flint
Description: Hard sedimentary rock that fractures with sharp edges. Essential for fire-starting and tool-making.

Name: Pumice
Description: Lightweight volcanic glass foam. Floats on water. Used as abrasive and for smoothing.
LiveValues: {"Description": "Magma cooled by air — so light it floats, full of trapped breath.", "Zone": "Campgrounds", "Category": "refined", "Rarity": "uncommon", "Base44Id": "6aa23879cd9fd41196298fe4", "CreatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000", "UpdatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000"}

Name: Quartz
Description: Clear to milky quartz crystal. Common but essential for resonance tuning and light focusing.

Name: Moonwood
Description: Pale wood that shimmers silver in moonlight. Grows only in Fae-touched groves.

Name: Rosewood
Description: Dark reddish-brown hardwood with tight grain. Prized for fine carving and inlay work.

Name: Thornwood
Description: Dark wood covered in sharp thorns. Harvested carefully — the thorns themselves are used in trap mechanisms.

Name: Driftwood
Description: Weathered wood washed ashore from distant seas. Salt-cured and uniquely shaped by waves.

Name: Mahogany
Description: Rich reddish-brown tropical hardwood. Dense, durable, and beautifully figured.

Name: Ebony
Description: Dense black wood, heavy and fine-grained. Takes polish beautifully. Used for inlay and dark accents.

Name: Ash
Description: Tough flexible wood with pale bark. Used for tool handles and bent-wood frameworks.
ClimateCycle: Garden sun — the standard the yard holds
CraftPairing: With Oak — the handle and the door
CraftProperty: Straight-grained, springy, splits true — the wood that takes the hand's force and gives it back
RitualRole: THE CONNECTION WOOD — handles and hafts; what joins the hand to the tool; the world-tree's own
LiveValues: {"Description": "Smoke quenched by water — the residue of fire, fertile and grey.", "Zone": "Campgrounds", "Category": "refined", "Rarity": "uncommon", "Base44Id": "6aa23879cd9fd41196298fe7", "CreatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000", "UpdatedDate": "2026-09-10T04:56:25.488000"}

Name: Cedar
Description: Aromatic reddish wood resistant to rot. Used for chest-making and sacred objects.
ClimateCycle: Norse highland cold — the slow-grown dense grain
CraftPairing: With Birch — the Norse storage pair
CraftProperty: Repels insects; endures decades without rotting
RitualRole: THE KEEPING WOOD — chests, coffins, and closets; purification by preservation (what cedar guards stays saved)

Name: Tin
Description: Soft silvery metal. Alloyed with copper to make bronze. Found in alluvial deposits.

Name: Mithril
Description: Silver-white magical metal lighter than steel but stronger. Resonates with frequency. Found only in Fae-touched veins.

Name: Thyme
Description: The guard herb of the Garden Path — the antiseptic planted beneath the rose.
ClimateCycle: Garden sun — the warming beds; the scent carries on the dry days
CraftPairing: Beneath the Rose — the guard and the guarded; the pairing layer's first lesson
CraftProperty: The field antiseptic — the herb of the wound and the kitchen; what it does is what it smells like doing
RitualRole: The guard — planted beneath the rose to keep it; the honest medicine of the field

Name: Rose
Description: The comforter of the Garden Path — petals for grief, hips for winter.
ClimateCycle: Garden sun and frost both — the hips need the winter to be medicine
CraftPairing: With Willow and Thyme — the mourning-tea trio; the grief tea's heart
CraftProperty: The heart-opener — the petal for grief tea, the hip for winter medicine (the vitamin the winter lacks)
RitualRole: The comforter — the grief tea with Willow; the garden's heart

Name: Rowan
Description: The protection wood of the mountain edges and the Fae borders — the tree that guards by being untempting.
ClimateCycle: The worst soil — the thin mountain edge where nothing else takes
CraftPairing: At the Fae borders — the rowan hedge between the courts; the mountain threshold planting
CraftProperty: Bitter berries; thrives in the worst soil; nothing eats it because nothing wants it
RitualRole: THE PROTECTION WOOD — the red-thread charm, the threshold planting against the unkind; the border-keeper earned by bitterness

Name: Indigo
Description: The dyer's plant — the deep blue of the India recipes, from the Garden Chhatri to the Royal Sandstone Palace.
ClimateCycle: India — the monsoon-fed warm lowlands; the vat likes the heat
CraftPairing: With Sandalwood and Teak — India's craft trio (the cloth, the scent, the frame)
CraftProperty: The blue that breathes — the leaf's green juice ferments to blue in the vat; the dye is living chemistry (the indigo vat is a tended garden of the blue)
RitualRole: The dyer's craft — the deep cloth's blue; the color that deepens with age instead of fading

Name: Heather
Description: The moor's gift to the roofline — Viking turf-pit-house thatch, Celtic wattle binding, the longbow range's hillside.
Source: Moorland heaths, Norse and Camelot borders
ClimateCycle: Norse moorland — the cold heath where nothing woody grows; the bees make the honey the moor allows
CraftPairing: With Bog Moss — the pit-house thatch pair; with Yew — the Norse Throne's weave
CraftProperty: The heath's own builder — tough stems, the bees' forage (the heather honey), thatch and rope from the stems; the ground-cover that makes soil where soil can't
RitualRole: The roof and the rope — the thatch that shrugs rain, the binding that holds the wattler's weave

Name: Resin
Description: The sealer of the Tier 1 builds — Pine Floor and Oak Wall gleam because the tree brought its own polish.
Source: Pine groves — any forest the pine claims
ClimateCycle: Cold-warm cycles — the sap runs when the warmth wakes the tree; the cold sets it hard
CraftPairing: With Pine — the floor pair; with Oak — the wall pair
CraftProperty: The tree's own medicine chest — the sap that seals wounds (the tree's and the builder's); antiseptic, sticky, the glue that was before glue
RitualRole: The Sealer — pitch and varnish, the joiner's grip, the torch's light; the finish that is gathered, not mixed

Name: Blackthorn
Description: The hedgerow's thorned boundary tree — the sloe's dark wood, the fae's own staff.
Source: Hedgerows, Camelot and the Fae borders
ClimateCycle: The hedgerow's edge — the frost that sweetens the sloe is the boundary climate (the field-side and the wild-side)
CraftPairing: With Rowan — the Fae borders' two guardians (the bitter and the thorned); the sloe gin with Heather honey
CraftProperty: So dense it sinks in water; the darkest heartwood; every branch armed with thorns; the sloe fruit that only sweetens after the first frost
RitualRole: THE HEDGE WOOD — the boundary tree: the hedgerow is the threshold line between field and wild; the thorn that keeps the wild out and the fae honest; the walking stick, the shillelagh, the Unseelie's black staff

Name: Kauri
Description: The Pacific giant — the waka's wood and the swamp-kept ancient.
Source: The Polynesian platform — kauri groves and swamp beds
ClimateCycle: The Polynesian platform — the warm rain and the swamp that keeps
CraftPairing: With Bog Oak — the two time-kept woods, hemispheres apart; with Resin — the weepers
CraftProperty: The giant that outlives nations; the swamp kauri — trees that fell 45,000 years ago and were KEPT (bog oak's Pacific kin); the gum that weeps amber's poor cousin
RitualRole: THE ANCIENT WOOD — the canoe tree (the waka); the wood older than the Inn's oldest shelves; the kauri gum is the Pacific's amber

Name: RedwoodCedar
Description: The giving tree of the Pacific coast — the rot-proof canoe and shingle wood.
Source: Pacific rain forests, the Redwood corridor
ClimateCycle: Pacific rain — the wet that tests every wood; the fog drip that feeds the roots
CraftPairing: With Redwood and Fog Moss — the canopy corridor's trio
CraftProperty: Rot-proof, light, splits true along the grain; the bark weaves and the wood breathes (the shingles that last a century in the rain)
RitualRole: THE GIVING TREE — the coastal peoples' tree of everything: canoes, poles, baskets, bark robes; cypress's Pacific cousin; the wood that holds no rot and asks no payment

Name: WitchHazel
Description: The winter-blooming finder — the dowsing switch and the distiller's bark.
ClimateCycle: Appalachian frost — the winter bloom; the understory shade
CraftPairing: With Ginseng — the mountain's two medicines; with Rowan — the finders and the keepers
CraftProperty: Blooms in the dead of winter when nothing else will; the forked switch that bends over hidden water (the dowsing rod); the bark's astringent chemistry — the distillation IS the medicine
RitualRole: THE FINDING WOOD — the water-witch's rod, the dowser's fork, the finder of what's hidden (springs, lost things — the Inn's own lost things); the flower when the world is asleep

Name: Ironwood
Description: The unyielding wood of the east — the tool part that must not wear.
ClimateCycle: Appalachian — the understory's slow growth makes the density
CraftPairing: With Ash — the connection and the unyielding; the handle pair; with Desert Ironwood — the two ironwoods, biomes apart
CraftProperty: So dense it dulls tools and sinks in water; the true ironwood of the east (the hornbeam) — the wood for the parts that must not wear (gear teeth, mallet heads, the wedges that split everything else)
RitualRole: THE UNYIELDING WOOD — the part that takes the pounding so the rest doesn't; the millwright's secret

Name: Madder
Description: THE RED — the dye wheel's first primary, the patience crop of the ancient dye gardens.
ClimateCycle: Mesopotamia — the warm dry; the three-year root (the patience crop: three seasons in the ground before the root is red enough)
CraftPairing: With Weld and Indigo — the wheel's three anchors; with Oak Gall — the mordant's hold
CraftProperty: The root's chemistry — the alizarin red: the dye that colored the ancient world's cloth; needs the mordant or it washes to pink (the chemistry is the honesty)
RitualRole: The wheel's first primary — the dye-garden's anchor; the red that holds when the mordant holds

Name: Weld
Description: THE YELLOW — the dye wheel's second primary, the light under every other color.
ClimateCycle: Greece — the dry hillsides; the first-year rosette, the second-year spike
CraftPairing: With Madder — the orange blend; with Indigo — the green dip
CraftProperty: The yellowest yellow the old world knew — the plant's own tops carry the luteolin; the dye the tapestries were built on (the yellow that holds for centuries)
RitualRole: The wheel's second primary — the light under every other color (the green and the orange both start here)

Name: Woad
Description: THE NORTH'S BLUE — the cold-weather twin of indigo, the wheel's blue where the trade roads don't reach.
ClimateCycle: Camelot — the cold that indigo can't take; woad grows where the blue must be local
CraftPairing: With Indigo — the blue cousins; with Madder — the purple dip (the north's own Tyrian)
CraftProperty: The indigo's cousin — the same blue chemistry from a cold-climate leaf (the blue the Celts painted with); the vat must ferment to breathe
RitualRole: The wheel's blue, northern branch — the war paint and the cloth

Name: OakGall
Description: THE FIXER — the mordant and the ink: what holds the dye to the cloth and the word to the page.
ClimateCycle: The hedgerow oak — the wound answers with the tannin; the dry late-summer drop
CraftPairing: With Bog Iron — the ink pair (the gall's tannin + the iron = the Archive's black); with every dye — the hold
CraftProperty: The oak's own wound — the gall wasp's nudge and the tree's answer: the tannin ball (among the highest tannin in nature); crushed with iron salts it is the iron-gall ink
RitualRole: The mordant — the hold every color needs; the scribes' black that lasts a thousand years (the Archive's own ink)

Name: Air
Description: The unseen carrier — wind, breath, the medium of sound.

Name: Brick
Description: Mud hardened by fire — the rectangular unit of every wall.

Name: Calcite
Description: Minerals precipitated by water over time — the builder of caves, bones, and shells.

Name: Ceramic
Description: Clay fired to permanence — the vessel, the tile, the shard of civilizations.

Name: Dust
Description: Stone scattered by wind — the finest grain, the quietest erosion.

Name: Fire
Description: The forge's breath — transforms, refines, destroys and creates.

Name: Geode
Description: Crystal growing inside stone — the secret interior, the Inn's namesake.

Name: Geyser
Description: Steam pressurized through stone — the earth's exhale, rhythmic and ancient.

Name: Glass
Description: Sand fused by fire — transparent, fragile, luminous.

Name: Lava
Description: Magma fed by more fire — the surface form of the deep melt.

Name: Magma
Description: Stone melted by fire — the earth's blood, waiting to cool.

Name: Mist
Description: Water carried by air — the veil between seen and unseen.

Name: Mud
Description: Dust saturated with water — the builder's first material.

Name: Pressure
Description: Stone compressed by magma — the tectonic force, the maker of sedimentary rock.

Name: Sand
Description: Stone worn by water — the beginning of glass, the end of mountains.

Name: Shale
Description: Mud compressed by pressure — the fissile stone, pages of geological history.

Name: Smoke
Description: Fire's breath in air — the sign of what was consumed.

Name: Steam
Description: Fire meeting water — the hiss of transformation, the engine of geysers.

Name: Stone
Description: The foundation of the earth — hard, patient, ancient.

Name: Time
Description: Stone ground to sand — the slow force, the calcifier, the preserver.

Name: Travertine
Description: Crystal deposited over time — the terrace stone, the cascading mineral.

Name: Tuff
Description: Ash compressed by pressure — the welded stone of volcanic plains.

Name: Water
Description: The solvent of worlds — shapes stone, feeds life, carries frequency.
